entries.snippet: The BBC asks Westerners who moved to Russia if life there lives up to expectations.

entries.title: As Supreme Court expands Trump's immigration power, experts warn of steeper U.S. population decline
entries.snippet: The U.S. population was already aging and tilting toward decline. After the Supreme Court confirmed Trump's power to deport hundreds of thousands of foreign migrants, population decline could accelerate.

entries.title: How coach Mauricio Pochettino made believers out of the U.S. World Cup team
entries.snippet: Pochettino was the biggest name the U.S. men's soccer team had ever hired. His rebuild was bumpy at times — but now, with the U.S. headed to the World Cup knockout stage, the players are all in.

entries.title: Inside a secretive Ukrainian team launching deep drone strikes at Russia
entries.snippet: Ukraine's long-range drones are striking deep inside Russia, up to 1,200 miles away, hitting oil refineries and depots. NPR recently spent time with one of the Ukrainian strike teams launching drones at Russian targets.

entries.title: 4 ways to get creative with your leftovers (and save money on food)
entries.snippet: Don't let your leftovers go to waste. Cookbook authors share clever storage techniques — like an "Eat Me First" box in your fridge — and cooking tricks to help you make the most of your food scraps.

entries.title: Venezuelans in Colombia scramble to send aid as earthquakes death toll increases
entries.snippet: Aid efforts are intensifying after twin earthquakes killed nearly 1,000 in Venezuela, with international teams arriving but a slow government response hampering relief on the ground.

entries.title: What would George Washington say? It's a busy year for people who portray him
entries.snippet: America's 250th birthday has brought more events and new crowds for Revolutionary reenactors and interpreters. They say Washington's life holds important lessons for our current political divide.

entries.title: There's a beef about beef at the World Cup, as Argentina fans pour into Texas
entries.snippet: It's about who produces the best, most succulent steaks, and how to prepare the meat. Argentina and Texas are two of the top cattle-raising areas of the world, where steak is deeply ingrained in diet and culture.

entries.title: U.S. strikes Iran in response to a drone attack on a ship
entries.snippet: The U.S. struck Iran on Friday in response to a drone attack a day earlier on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz. It's the most significant test yet to an interim understanding reached a week ago by the two countries.

entries.title: Apple increases prices for Macs and iPads, blaming memory chip shortage fueled by AI
entries.snippet: The Cupertino, California-based company called the demand spike an "unprecedented challenge" for the consumer electronics industry.

entries.title: Americans are inundated with suspected scams. New polls show why few victims report them
entries.snippet: Most Americans are inundated with scam attempts on a daily basis — and about 3 in 10 have personally lost money or personal information to scams, according to a new AP-NORC survey.

entries.title: DNC plans weekend of local events to focus on affordability concerns under Trump
entries.snippet: Two years ago, Democrats were the ones accused of being indifferent to Americans' anger about rising prices. Now they're pointing the finger at Trump, who has downplayed the impact of lingering inflation.

entries.title: Crews race to find survivors in mountains of rubble after Venezuela earthquakes

entries.snippet: The WNBA has suspended Phoenix's Alyssa Thomas for one game after she made contact with her fist to Caitlin Clark's throat in Wednesday night's matchup against Indiana.

entries.snippet: On Friday, the U.S. military conducted new strikes against Iran in response to what President Trump said was Tehran's violation of the ceasefire. Nick Schifirin reports.

entries.snippet: Putin and Ivanov knew each other since the 1970s when they both worked as young KGB officers in their hometown of Leningrad, as St. Petersburg was called during the Soviet times.

entries.snippet: Heated games and rough plays sparked a new controversy in the WNBA around its superstar Caitlin Clark. The Phoenix Mercury's Alyssa Thomas pressed her fist into Clark's neck during a game. The league retroactively gave Thomas a flagrant foul and suspended her for one game. But qu

entries.title: Black Opera Project celebrates resilience and richness of the Black American experience

entries.snippet: The strikes came shortly after Trump told reporters, "You'll find out," whether the U.S. would respond to a drone attack a day earlier on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: Texas education board approves Bible stories as required reading in public schools
entries.snippet: The Texas education board on Friday approved a required reading list for more than 5 million public school students that includes Bible passages, widening conservative efforts to push Christian teachings in U.S. classrooms.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump receives report from Religious Liberty Commission in the Oval Office
entries.snippet: A new report by a Trump administration commission suggests replacing the idea of separating church and state with the idea of building bridges between them.

entries.title: Live Results: Louisiana midterm primary runoffs
entries.snippet: Louisiana Republicans will nominate a candidate for U.S. Senate in a primary runoff Saturday, six weeks after denying Republican U.S. Sen. Bill Cassidy a shot at a third term.

entries.title: Newsom urges a national 'billionaires' tax' while fighting one in California
entries.snippet: The governor announced his agenda a day after an influential health care union in California pledged to go forward with a ballot measure that would impose a one-time 5% tax on the assets of billionaires living in the state as of Jan. 1, 2026. Newsom opposes that measure.

entries.title: Heat catches Europe's fashion industry unprepared as models face the sun in fur and wool
entries.snippet: The most coveted accessory at the Paris Fashion Week shows this week was not a bag, a sneaker or a watch. It was an ice pack.

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Germany news: Heat soars as political reforms split opinion
entries.snippet: As Europe's heatwave rages, Germany continues to swelter with new records expected Saturday. Elsewhere, politicians bicker over reforms and industry blames train operator DB for billions in losses. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Why Germany's Deutsche Bahn will face delays for many years
entries.snippet: Delayed, unreliable and forced into long detours due to construction: Germany no longer sets the pace when it comes to rail travel — and this is unlikely to change anytime soon. The company is mired in a deep crisis.

entries.title: Military-age Ukrainian men could lose EU protection
entries.snippet: The European Commission has suggested withdrawing protection status for military-age Ukrainian males. A number of EU countries support the move — and so does Kyiv.

entries.title: Europe faces scorching weekend as heat wave moves east
entries.snippet: Europe's heat wave is expected to move east after causing record temperatures in several countries. But Germany still has a couple of torrid days ahead. DW has the latest.

entries.title: India news: PM Modi embarks on two-day Seychelles visit
entries.snippet: India's PM Narendra Modi is set to be the Guest of Honor at the Golden Jubilee of Seychelles' National Day. His visit is also aimed at stregnthening martime, security and economic cooperation. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Comedy legend Mel Brooks turns 100
entries.snippet: A parody of Adolf Hitler in the landmark 1968 movie "The Producers" was just the beginning for US actor Mel Brooks. The 100-year-old comedian is still on a roll today.

entries.title: Court upholds Weinstein rape conviction
entries.snippet: A California court has upheld the conviction of disgraced movie mogul Harvey Weinstein but said a lower court judge must resentence him. Allegations against Weinstein sparked the #MeToo movement.

entries.title: US, Iran trade strikes as truce faces threat
entries.snippet: The United States and Iran each launched strikes in the worst escalation since they signed their interim peace deal. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Trump foe John Bolton pleads guilty in classified docs case
entries.snippet: Bolton faces as many as five years in prison. He had earlier served as Trump's national security adviser during the president's first term in office, but later resigned over his differences with Trump.

entries.title: US, Lebanon, Israel sign framework agreement
entries.snippet: US Secretary ‌of ⁠State ⁠Marco ​Rubio has announced ​a trilateral ​framework ‌agreement. Lebanese officials began direct talks with Israel in Washington in April.

entries.title: Creative climate messaging and other eco wins of the week
entries.snippet: An artist in Mali and climate scientists in the US are finding new ways to inform the public about the climate crisis.

entries.title: Fact check: Throwing cold water on heat wave disinformation
entries.snippet: An outdated air-conditioning law, a viral health myth about sleeping with the fan on and the age-old climate change hoax allegation: DW checked what's spreading in Europe's heat wave.

entries.title: World Cup: Morocco's Ismael Saibari set for Bayern Munich
entries.snippet: Three nationalities, five languages and soon to be resident in a fourth country: Ismael Saibari, the star of Morocco's World Cup so far, is set to join Bayern Munich. But he has business to finish with the Atlas Lions.

entries.title: German lawyers: Ban on far-right AfD 'likely successful'
entries.snippet: A new report by legal experts has found that efforts to ban Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) could be successful — but there would be political dangers to such a move.

entries.title: 'Operation Purgatory': Magyar moves to demolish Orban system
entries.snippet: The new Hungarian government is moving swiftly to dismantle the system of former PM Viktor Orban. The focus is on fighting corruption, reforming the media and protecting democracy.

entries.title: How the Iran war has disrupted Abu Dhabi's AI strategy
entries.snippet: Abu Dhabi's ambitions to turn the United Arab Emirates into a global hub for digital infrastructure and artificial Intelligence face pressure after the Iran war. But the country is also known for its business resilience.

entries.title: World Cup: 'Pride Match' sparks objections in Egypt and Iran
entries.snippet: Friday night's game in Seattle was designated as a "Pride Match" well ahead of the World Cup draw. The fixture list then threw up Egypt vs. Iran, two countries in which homosexuality is criminalized.

entries.title: India news: Government sends help to quake-hit Venezuela
entries.snippet: Two air force planes carrying supplies as well as a field hospital unit are on their way. Also making headlines: Qatar has repatriated the bodies of four Indians killed in a gas explosion. DW has more.

entries.title: Wagner festival reinstates Holocaust memorial event after cancellation
entries.snippet: The Bayreuth Festival had canceled a planned memorial lecture featuring Jewish author and broadcaster Michel Friedman, drawing sharp criticism.
